summary.intent: Unblock and land the open caliper PR stack (red CI, approvals gate, stacked-PR retargeting), then plan the next caliper work and produce a handoff prompt for a new session focused on closing the v1 alpha gap (accuracy gaps + TS 7.1 on-demand).
summary.outcome: All stack PRs (#258, #259, #260, #261, #264) merged and main CI went green; only release PR #239 remained, with the user running the release. A full handoff prompt was produced with the schema v4 batch ordered first, but the weekly baseline and v4 work have not started.

repo: Entire Gates enforces an `approvals` gate that fails with 'No reviewers have approved this trail'; agents must not self-approve. Approve with `entire trail approve <n> --project gh/orin-dx` or in the Entire UI.
The main ruleset requires 1 approving review, signed commits, the merge queue and non-fast-forward protection. Only merge commits are allowed (squash and rebase are off).

A PR in an Entire stack cannot be retargeted after its parent merges (GitHub returns 'Cannot change the base branch because the pull request is part of a stack'). #262 was stuck on a dead base, so the same branch was re-homed onto #261 targeting main.
Entire auto-creates a draft PR when you run `entire trail link`; fill that PR in with gh pr edit/ready rather than opening a second one.
Lint and CI on #258, #260 and #264 were red only because main's lint was red. Merging the lint fix branch (adding `.oxfmtrc.json`) cleared them.
Bot-generated PRs like release PR #239 don't trigger CI on their head commit. The merge queue runs the checks, which is why #264 added the `merge_group` trigger.

Homebrew tap is pull-based: its daily `brew bump` follows `npm/caliper-docgen@*` tags and builds from source. The old `notify-homebrew-tap` push step with `TAP_APP_*` was obsolete and removed by #258.
Measurement is now a single weekly workflow (`scripts/weekly.py`) plus `just bench`; the PR gates were deleted and should not be rebuilt.
workflow: Forks and parallel agents need `isolation: "worktree"`; two agents in one worktree clobber each other.
Run git with the sandbox off and keep commits GPG-signed; unsigned fork commits previously forced a re-sign force-push.
Don't pipe lint or test output through tail/head, since a pipe once hid a real failure; read exit codes directly.
Warn up front that 'GitHub retargets to main' does not hold for PRs in Entire stacks. Prefer independent PRs off main.
Verify an assumption like `weekly.yml` supporting `workflow_dispatch` before putting it in a handoff prompt.

friction: Merge of #262 failed because of the stale stacked base. The exact error text was never captured, so the cause (base vs review vs ruleset) wasn't confirmed.
The one-person team hits its own approvals gate on every PR, leaving the agent unable to unblock merges.
Merge-queue checks never reported on `gh-readonly-queue/*` branches until #264, which likely stalled merges.
Nothing merged for days, and main's red lint cascaded into red CI on every dependent PR.
The 'final gap for v1 alpha' was undefined at first and needed clarification before the handoff was useful.
open_items: Release #239 (0.7.0 to 0.8.0) is in progress; watch Release & Publish, tags, npm and crates.io, and the tap's brew bump. It is the first real run of Callisto 0.16.0.
Run the weekly workflow by hand for a fresh baseline; the quoted numbers are stale one-machine figures.
Ship the schema v4 batch (readonly, index signatures, RefObject) in one PR with a migration changeset.
Root-cause and fix the shadcn and antd recall gaps by shape; check whether antd PurePanel's 33 props are a harness pairing bug.
Detection by shape: memo(forwardRef(function...)) without type args, React APIs by import source, the {Name}Props rule, and Chakra NonNullable<union>.
Harden TS 7.1 on-demand: version range with self-check, memory cap, real-tsc CI test, and optionally a disk cache.
Create trails (a to d) with acceptance criteria before any branch.
User-owned housekeeping: delete remote scratch branches, remove `TAP_APP_*` secrets if set, close stale trails, and clean up local worktrees and branches (lf-258, lf-260, rc-*, cc-*).
Decide whether to keep the Human Review approvals gate or turn it off in Gates settings.
Confirm nobody has a bypass on main's force-push protection.
